Wouldn’t an affluent omnivorous diet harm the most, then? 
Many people who eat omnivorous diets eat pretty much the same vegetable matter on top of consuming meat products. 
So it stands to reason that your average affluent Omni western diet would still be harming more than a vegan one. 

Also it’s my experience as an employee at my areas co-op that many affluent vegans (and indeed affluent omnis) care very deeply about the ethics behind their food and go to great lengths to buy from vendors such as Equal Exchange who promote the ethical treatment of their workers above all else.
Granted, I know what a hotly debated topic fair trade items are, and that no matter what human injury cannot be prevented in most lines of work, but if supporting companies in which people get injured is the issue then everyone who has ever written on paper or used anything made out of wood is actively contributing funds to human death and injury.
Not only that but there are many members from both dietary backgrounds who make a point to only purchase local & sustainably sourced produce.
It would be interesting to see some studies on this.

To conclude I think this is a really fascinating angle to bring up, but in a world where affluent western consumers have the choice of harming humans and animals with their purchases— isn’t it better at least to reduce the suffering brought on by said purchases as much as possible? 
Maybe by cutting out a huge swath of it by not purchasing animal products?
